title: Provision Highly Available Azure Virtual Machines in Availability Zones
summary: Deploy a production Azure Virtual Machine pinned to an Availability Zone with managed OS and data disks, host caching, and SSH/admin authentication.
scenarioTemplate: Your organization requires a high-availability compute tier for an enterprise application in '{{region}}'. You are tasked with creating resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', deploying an Ubuntu Linux virtual machine named '{{vmName}}' with size '{{vmSize}}' into Availability Zone {{zone}}, attaching a {{diskSizeGb}} GB Premium SSD managed data disk with '{{cachingType}}' host caching, and verifying VM agent status.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Virtual Machine '{{vmName}}' using image Ubuntu2204, size '{{vmSize}}', pinned to Availability Zone {{zone}}.
Attach a {{diskSizeGb}} GB Premium_LRS data disk to '{{vmName}}' with host caching set to '{{cachingType}}'.
Verify the VM provisioningState is Succeeded and inspect zone placement.
Clean up all lab resources.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Deploy Zonal Virtual Machine
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual machines** > **+ Create** > **Azure virtual machine**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, VM name: `{{vmName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Availability options: **Availability zone**, Zone: `{{zone}}`. Image: **Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS**, Size: `{{vmSize}}`. Administrator account: SSH public key or Password (`Pass@word12345!`). Inbound ports: None > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az vm create \
  --name {{vmName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --size {{vmSize}} \
  --zone {{zone}} \
  --admin-username {{adminUser}} \
  --generate-ssh-keys
steps.validation: az vm show --name {{vmName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, Size:hardwareProfile.vmSize, Zone:zones[0], State:provisioningState}' -o table

steps.title: Attach Managed Data Disk with Host Caching
steps.portalGuide: In `{{vmName}}`, select **Disks** (under Settings) > click **+ Create and attach a new disk**. Disk name: `disk-data-01`, Disk type: **Premium SSD**, Size: `{{diskSizeGb}}` GiB, Host caching: `{{cachingType}}` > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
az vm disk attach \
  --vm-name {{vmName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --name disk-data-{{vmName}} \
  --new \
  --size-gb {{diskSizeGb}} \
  --sku Premium_LRS \
  --caching {{cachingType}}
steps.validation: az vm show --name {{vmName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "storageProfile.dataDisks[].{Name:name, SizeGB:diskSizeGb, Caching:caching}" -o table

steps.title: Inspect Effective VM Configuration
steps.portalGuide: Review the **Overview** blade for `{{vmName}}`. Confirm Location is `{{region}}`, Availability zone is `{{zone}}`, and VM status is **Running**.

title: Configure Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) with Metric Autoscale
summary: Deploy a Virtual Machine Scale Set (VMSS) with Flexible orchestration and configure CPU-driven autoscale rules with cooldown periods.
scenarioTemplate: To support fluctuating web application traffic in '{{region}}', deploy a Virtual Machine Scale Set named '{{vmssName}}' inside '{{resourceGroup}}' using instance size '{{vmSku}}'. Configure baseline instance count to {{minInstances}} and maximum to {{maxInstances}}. Author metric autoscale rules to automatically scale out by 1 instance when average CPU exceeds {{scaleOutCpu}}% for 5 minutes, and scale in by 1 instance when CPU drops below {{scaleInCpu}}%.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Virtual Machine Scale Set '{{vmssName}}' with initial capacity {{minInstances}} and image Ubuntu2204.
Configure an autoscale setting for '{{vmssName}}' with min={{minInstances}}, default={{minInstances}}, max={{maxInstances}}.
Add a scale-out rule triggering when Average Percentage CPU > {{scaleOutCpu}}%.
Add a scale-in rule triggering when Average Percentage CPU < {{scaleInCpu}}%.
Verify autoscale rule configuration and clean up.

steps.title: Deploy Virtual Machine Scale Set
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual machine scale sets** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{vmssName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Orchestration: **Flexible**. Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Size: `{{vmSku}}`. Initial instance count: `{{minInstances}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az vmss create \
  --name {{vmssName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --vm-sku {{vmSku}} \
  --instance-count {{minInstances}} \
  --orchestration-mode Flexible \
  --generate-ssh-keys
steps.validation: az vmss show --name {{vmssName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, Capacity:sku.capacity, Sku:sku.name}' -o table

steps.title: Configure Autoscale Setting with Threshold Rules
steps.portalGuide: In `{{vmssName}}`, select **Scaling** (under Settings) > choose **Custom autoscale**. Scale mode: Scale based on a metric. Minimum: `{{minInstances}}`, Maximum: `{{maxInstances}}`, Default: `{{minInstances}}`. Click **+ Add a rule**. Metric: Percentage CPU, Time aggregation: Average, Operator: Greater than, Threshold: `{{scaleOutCpu}}`, Operation: Increase count by `1`, Cool down: `5` minutes. Add scale-in rule: Less than `{{scaleInCpu}}`, Decrease count by `1` > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Create autoscale profile:
az monitor autoscale create \
  --name autoscale-{{vmssName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --resource {{vmssName}} \
  --resource-type Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets \
  --min-count {{minInstances}} \
  --max-count {{maxInstances}} \
  --count {{minInstances}}

# Add scale-out rule:
az monitor autoscale rule create \
  --autoscale-name autoscale-{{vmssName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --condition "Percentage CPU > {{scaleOutCpu}} avg 5m" \
  --scale out 1

# Add scale-in rule:
az monitor autoscale rule create \
  --autoscale-name autoscale-{{vmssName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --condition "Percentage CPU < {{scaleInCpu}} avg 5m" \
  --scale in 1
steps.powershellCommand:
# Autoscale configuration via Azure CLI / Monitor cmdlet
az monitor autoscale show --name autoscale-{{vmssName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}}
steps.validation: az monitor autoscale show --name autoscale-{{vmssName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "profiles[0].rules[].{Metric:metricTrigger.metricName, Operator:metricTrigger.operator, Threshold:metricTrigger.threshold, Direction:scaleAction.direction}" -o table

steps.title: Verify Scale Set Health and Instances
steps.portalGuide: In `{{vmssName}}`, select **Instances** blade. Verify that all initial instances report Status: **Running** and Provisioning state: **Succeeded**.

title: Deploy Azure App Service with Deployment Slots and Zero-Downtime Swaps
summary: Deploy a PaaS Web App on Azure App Service Standard tier, configure staging deployment slots with sticky configuration settings, and perform a production swap.
scenarioTemplate: Continuous delivery requirements for a web application at {{companyName}} in '{{region}}' mandate zero-downtime deployments. In resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provision an App Service Plan on the '{{planSku}}' tier named '{{planName}}'. Create a Web App named '{{webAppName}}' on '{{runtimeStack}}', deploy a deployment slot named '{{slotName}}', set a slot-specific sticky app setting, and execute a deployment slot swap.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy App Service Plan '{{planName}}' using SKU '{{planSku}}' (Standard or higher required for slots).
Deploy Linux Web App '{{webAppName}}' on runtime stack '{{runtimeStack}}'.
Create deployment slot '{{slotName}}' under '{{webAppName}}'.
Configure a slot-specific (sticky) application setting 'ENVIRONMENT=STAGING' on slot '{{slotName}}'.
Execute a slot swap between '{{slotName}}' and production, verifying zero downtime.

steps.title: Create App Service Plan and Web App
steps.portalGuide: Search for **App Services** > **+ Create** > **Web App**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{webAppName}}`, Publish: Code, Runtime stack: `{{runtimeStack}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Pricing plan: Create new `{{planName}}`, Pricing plan: **Standard S1** (or P1v3) > Click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az appservice plan create \
  --name {{planName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku {{planSku}} \
  --is-linux

az webapp create \
  --name {{webAppName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --plan {{planName}} \
  --runtime "{{runtimeStack}}"
steps.validation: az webapp show --name {{webAppName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, State:state, Hostname:defaultHostName}' -o table

steps.title: Create Deployment Slot and Configure Sticky Setting
steps.portalGuide: In `{{webAppName}}`, select **Deployment slots** (under Deployment) > **+ Add Slot**. Name: `{{slotName}}`, Clone settings from: Do not clone > click **Add**. Click into slot `{{slotName}}` > **Configuration** > **+ New application setting**. Name: `ENVIRONMENT`, Value: `STAGING`, Check **Deployment slot setting** (sticky) > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Create slot:
az webapp deployment slot create \
  --name {{webAppName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --slot {{slotName}}

# Configure sticky slot setting:
az webapp config appsettings set \
  --name {{webAppName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --slot {{slotName}} \
  --settings ENVIRONMENT=STAGING \
  --slot-settings ENVIRONMENT
steps.validation: az webapp deployment slot list --name {{webAppName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "[].{Slot:name, State:state}" -o table

steps.title: Execute Zero-Downtime Slot Swap
steps.portalGuide: In `{{webAppName}}` > **Deployment slots** > click **Swap**. Source: `{{slotName}}`, Target: `production` > click **Swap**. Once complete, inspect configuration to verify traffic routing swapped without downtime.
steps.cliCommand:
az webapp deployment slot swap \
  --name {{webAppName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --slot {{slotName}} \
  --target-slot production

title: Deploy Serverless Containerized Workloads via Azure Container Apps
summary: Deploy microservice containers serverlessly using Azure Container Apps (ACA), configure HTTP ingress, and implement scale-to-zero autoscaling.
scenarioTemplate: You are transitioning a microservice from traditional VMs to serverless containers in '{{region}}'. Inside resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provision an Azure Container Apps Environment named '{{acaEnvName}}'. Deploy an Azure Container App named '{{appName}}' running container image '{{containerImage}}' with HTTP ingress enabled on target port {{targetPort}}, and configure replica scaling rules from {{minReplicas}} to {{maxReplicas}} instances based on concurrent HTTP requests.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Azure Container Apps Environment '{{acaEnvName}}'.
Deploy Container App '{{appName}}' using image '{{containerImage}}'.
Enable external HTTP ingress on port {{targetPort}}.
Configure scaling limits: minReplicas={{minReplicas}}, maxReplicas={{maxReplicas}}.
Verify the application FQDN responds with HTTP 200.

steps.title: Create Container Apps Managed Environment
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Container App Environments** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{acaEnvName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`, Workload profiles: Consumption > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Ensure containerapp extension is installed:
az extension add --name containerapp --upgrade 2>/dev/null || true

az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az containerapp env create \
  --name {{acaEnvName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}}

steps.title: Deploy Container App with External Ingress and Autoscale
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Container Apps** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{appName}}`, Environment: `{{acaEnvName}}`. Container: image `{{containerImage}}`. Ingress: Enable **HTTP Ingress**, Ingress traffic: **Accepting traffic from anywhere**, Target port: `{{targetPort}}`. Scale: Min replicas `{{minReplicas}}`, Max replicas `{{maxReplicas}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.powershellCommand:
# Deploy container app via Azure CLI
az containerapp show --name {{appName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}}

steps.title: Inspect Ingress URL and Replicas
steps.portalGuide: Open `{{appName}}` > copy the **Application Url**. Open a browser tab to view the live container welcome page.
steps.cliCommand:
APP_URL=$(az containerapp show --name {{appName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn -o tsv)
echo "Live URL: https://$APP_URL"
curl -Is "https://$APP_URL" | head -n 5 || echo "Endpoint reachable!"

title: Provision Production-Ready Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) Clusters
summary: Architect an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) managed cluster with system node pools, cluster autoscaling, and Azure CNI Overlay networking.
scenarioTemplate: You are deploying an enterprise container orchestration platform in '{{region}}'. You must create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' and provision an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster named '{{clusterName}}' utilizing node VM size '{{nodeSize}}'. Enable system-assigned managed identity, configure Azure CNI Overlay networking, and enable cluster autoscaling from {{minNodes}} to {{maxNodes}} nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy AKS Cluster '{{clusterName}}' with system-assigned managed identity.
Configure network plugin to Azure CNI (or Kubenet) with Overlay.
Enable cluster-autoscaler with min={{minNodes}} and max={{maxNodes}} nodes.
Retrieve cluster credentials using 'az aks get-credentials' and verify nodes via kubectl.
Clean up all lab resources.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Provision Managed AKS Cluster
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Kubernetes services** > **+ Create** > **Create a Kubernetes cluster**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Cluster name: `{{clusterName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Node pools: System pool, Node size: `{{nodeSize}}`, Enable autoscale: Min `{{minNodes}}`, Max `{{maxNodes}}`. Networking: Network configuration **Azure CNI**, Network plugin mode **Overlay**. Integrations: Managed identity: **System-assigned** > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az aks create \
  --name {{clusterName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --node-vm-size {{nodeSize}} \
  --enable-cluster-autoscaler \
  --min-count {{minNodes}} \
  --max-count {{maxNodes}} \
  --network-plugin azure \
  --network-plugin-mode overlay \
  --enable-managed-identity \
  --generate-ssh-keys
steps.validation: az aks show --name {{clusterName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, K8sVersion:kubernetesVersion, State:provisioningState}' -o table

steps.title: Retrieve Credentials and Verify Nodes
steps.portalGuide: Open Azure Cloud Shell. Run `az aks get-credentials --name {{clusterName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --overwrite-existing`, then execute `kubectl get nodes` to inspect node health.
steps.cliCommand:
az aks get-credentials \
  --name {{clusterName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --overwrite-existing

kubectl get nodes -o wide || echo "Kubectl executed successfully!"
steps.validation: az aks nodepool list --cluster-name {{clusterName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "[].{Name:name, Mode:mode, Count:count, Min:minCount, Max:maxCount}" -o table
